TL;DR: Codex is a multi-surface coding agent: it reads your codebase, runs commands in an OS-level sandbox, patches files, and delegates tasks to the cloud. Master five systems – config.toml, the sandbox/approval model, AGENTS.md, MCP, and skills – and it becomes a force multiplier. GPT-6-Astra is the new recommended default (launched September 3, 2026; the bundled CLI default as of v0.153.4) – OpenAI announced the rollout complete on September 4 (Plus and Business included by evening), but entitlement is still uneven in practice, so accounts not yet entitled should pin GPT-5.6 Sol (the “Power” setting, medium reasoning) as the stable fallback; GPT-5.5, the previous-generation flagship, offers 400K context in Codex and 1M in the API.[83](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:160)[117](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:201)[145](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:231)[146](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:232)[148](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:234)[149](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:235) New here? Jump straight to [Install](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#how-do-i-install-codex) and [Quick Start](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#quick-start-your-first-session). Tracking releases? The latest stable is v0.156.0 (September 22, 2026), the release that turns TUI voice conversations, managed worktrees, and Guardian parent-compaction reuse ON BY DEFAULT[169](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:247) – see [Release Highlights](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#release-highlights-what-changed-recently) for the recent-version narrative and the [Changelog](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#changelog) for every update.[116](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:200)
Codex operates as a multi-surface coding agent, not a chatbot that writes code. The CLI reads your codebase, executes commands in a sandbox, patches files, connects to external services via MCP, and delegates long-running tasks to the cloud. It runs locally but thinks globally; the same intelligence powers five distinct surfaces depending on how you work, including the browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi) that runs Codex in your browser without taking it over.[90](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:167)[127](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:213)
The difference between casual and effective Codex usage comes down to five core systems. Master these and Codex becomes a force multiplier:
Configuration system: controls behavior via config.toml
Sandbox & approval model: gates what Codex can do
AGENTS.md: defines project-level operating contracts
MCP protocol: extends capabilities to external services
Skills system: packages reusable domain expertise
I spent months running Codex alongside Claude Code across production codebases, CI/CD pipelines, and team workflows. This guide distills that experience into the complete reference I wish existed when I started. Every feature includes actual syntax, real configuration examples, and the edge cases that trip up experienced users.
Key Takeaways
Five surfaces, one brain: CLI, desktop app, IDE extension, cloud tasks, and the browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi) all share the same GPT-5.x-Codex intelligence, so pick the surface that fits your workflow.[90](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:167)
OS-level sandboxing: Codex enforces filesystem and network restrictions at the kernel level (Seatbelt on macOS, Landlock + seccomp on Linux), not inside containers.
AGENTS.md is cross-tool: Your project instructions work in Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Amp, Jules, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Cline, Aider, Zed, and 60,000+ open source projects. Write once, use everywhere.
Profiles save context-switching overhead: Define named config presets (fast, careful, auto) and switch between them with --profile.
Context management matters: the GPT-5.6 family (Sol, Terra, Luna) runs a 272K context window; GPT-5.5, the previous-generation flagship, provides 400K in Codex and 1M in the API. Use /compact, focused prompts, and @file references to manage token budgets proactively.[83](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:160)[112](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:194)

Release Highlights: What Changed Recently
The version-by-version narrative, for readers tracking Codex’s release train. New here? Skip this and come back after Quick Start – nothing in it is required to get productive.
GPT-6-Astra is the recommended Codex model – launched September 3, 2026, in a phased rollout (a limited set of organizations first, cybersecurity-program partners at the front) that OpenAI announced substantially complete the next day: an OpenAI post on X (September 4) states Astra “is now available to all Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users in ChatGPT Work and Codex” and “live in the API,” and the Codex lead Tibo Sottiaux followed up the same evening that “Astra is now rolled out to all Plus and Business users too.” Entitlement is still uneven in practice – September 5 community reports show Plus accounts seeing only GPT-5.6 models in Codex, and the models docs still say availability “depends on the rollout, your sign-in method, and your client” – so GPT-5.6 Sol (the “Power” setting, medium reasoning, adjustable toward Smarter or Faster) stays the stable recommendation for accounts where Astra does not yet answer; GPT-5.5 (April 23, 2026: 400K context in Codex, 1M in the API, $5/$30 per MTok, 82.7% Terminal-Bench 2.0 SOTA) is the previous-generation flagship.[83](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:160)[117](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:201)[145](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:231)[146](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:232)[149](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:235) v0.156.0 (stable, September 22, 2026, 19:51 UTC; npm latest at 19:55 UTC) is the release where three defaults flip at once: TUI voice conversations, managed worktrees, and Guardian parent-compaction reuse are all ON BY DEFAULT. Each flip was ancestry-checked against the tag rather than read off the body: “Enable TUI voice conversations by default” (#44921, merge 3f59eb9), “Enable worktrees by default and clarify local daemon errors” (#44870, merge 68bc536), and “Enable Guardian parent-compaction reuse by default” (#46522, merge 3fd9e7e). The consequence for readers of this guide’s earlier releases: the opt-in experimental framing that stood from v0.155.0 inverts. On 0.156.0, /voice works without a visit to /experimental on a supported build, managed worktrees are the default rather than a flag, and Guardian reuses the parent thread’s compaction. The rust-v0.155.1…rust-v0.156.0 compare is 526 commits. This release body is unusually substantial for this repo (roughly 43.8KB, a curated New Features section plus a full PR enumeration), and it makes a good discovery index, but the house rule holds: every item here was verified against the compare, not taken from the body. The cut itself is the lesson: 0.156.0 is a LATE cut, not the skip this guide recorded that morning. Compare-verified, the stable tag carries exactly the rust-v0.156.0-alpha.16 content (the two differ by one commit in each direction, each side’s own version bump), and alpha.16 published September 21 at 16:51 UTC, seventy-seven minutes before rust-v0.157.0-alpha.1 opened the successor line at 18:08 UTC. The release branch was cut from a base the alpha train had already moved past, then tagged September 22 at 18:39 UTC and published at 19:51, by which point nine 0.157.0-alpha cuts had shipped. A familiar branch cut sits on top of the late one: the two later cuts on the 0.156 alpha line missed stable entirely, with 21 commits in alpha.17 and 65 in alpha.18 that are not in rust-v0.156.0. All fifteen accumulated 0.156.0-alpha watch items shipped, with no reversals, and the release’s biggest user-visible surface was never on the watch list at all: an optional fullscreen TUI. /tui chooses the terminal UI mode for your next launch (#46883), and the alternate-screen mode brings a real transcript viewer with search and per-activity detail controls (#46734), mouse selection and copying (#46732, #46858), right-click copy for transcript and composer selections (#46895), plain clicks on transcript links with bare URLs styled (#46884), and a warning footer with a dedicated warnings viewer (#46751); fullscreen transcript control lives in TUI configuration and stays off by default in this release (#46849). The watch list, item by item: six bundled TUI themes with theme-aware accents (#46504) and catalog model display names throughout the TUI (#46503); the /usage account analytics dashboard (#45763, #45764, #45765, #45766, #45768, #45769, #45770, #45772) with its maturation pass for keyboard help, mouse navigation, and preserved reading positions (#46863, #46864, #46866) – note that #45767 and #45771 are not pull requests at all, so the “#45763-#45772” range this guide carried on the watch line is eight PRs, not ten; TUI Mermaid rendering (#45817, #46054, with stadium nodes added in #46856) and TeX math rendered as Unicode (#45501, #45612, #46266), both now behind independent rendering toggles alongside tables (#46938); the /daemon menu (#45854), the --no-daemon flag (#46088), and opt-in automatic background server startup (#46117), with local background servers identified in /status (#46905); voice maturation (the configurable F8 shortcut #46071, voice-session analytics #46058, a /voice settings picker #44622, bundled Linux and Windows voice runtimes #44714 and #44922, reduced motion #46835, and playback preserved across pauses and packet bursts #46880); worktree sessions on an existing local daemon (#46498), with worktree creation from the agents overview (#45276); reasoning summaries disabled by default for new TUI threads (#46533, agreeing with the 0.155.1 hotfix); bounded filesystem path diagnostics in codex doctor (#46543); the personality feature flag retired, with the deprecated friendly and pragmatic settings documented as no longer selecting a response style (#45809); daybreakEnabled on thread start (#45513), which gained no docs surface and no public explanation, so Daybreak stays code-only; and the Astra composer starfield (#46096). New and unwatched beyond the fullscreen TUI: a local agent message board arrives as working infrastructure rather than groundwork (SQLite storage #46966, paginated queries #46978, timestamp indexing #46979, collaboration tools #46985, shared extension interfaces #46959, delivery routed through captured send requests #46994); subagents can request MCP elicitation input (#46877); tool restrictions are decoupled from session identity by a new ToolPolicy (#46999); the agent command center gains status filter tabs plus row, navigation, and shortcut work (#46839, #46837, #46838, #46840, #46882); and the default terminal probe timeout moves from 100 ms to 250 ms (#46855). Security: non-loopback inbound traffic is blocked for the Windows offline sandbox (#44639), privileged Linux and macOS socket gaps are closed (#45984), writes through read-only macOS file handles are stopped (#46500), and codex doctor no longer exposes config values in its errors (#46962). Fixes worth knowing: streamed answers and plans survive failed, interrupted, and subagent-completed turns (#45549, #46867); clipboard forwarding works in tmux and SSH sessions (#45457) and tab indentation survives keystroke-style pastes (#45454); Plan mode is restored on resume (#45519) and thread identity and settings survive editing an earlier prompt (#45845); and login recovers through system proxies (#46562). Docs check, and this is the fastest the docs have moved in this guide’s tracking window: the ChatGPT and Codex changelog carried a dated Codex CLI 0.156.0 entry on 2026-09-22, the same day as the release, with the matching npm install -g @openai/codex@0.156.0 line, and it states the flip in first-party words: “Voice conversations are enabled by default, with an F8 toggle, a /voice settings picker, and bundled audio runtimes for Linux and Windows” and “worktree support is now enabled by default”. That is direct corroboration of both headline flips, and it supersedes the v0.155.0 entry’s “enabled through /experimental” framing. The reference pages lag the changelog, so state the gap plainly: the CLI developer-commands reference now lists /experimental without naming voice among its examples, and lists /usage, but /voice, /tui, and /daemon are still absent, as is --no-daemon from the flags table; the config reference has no features.voice, features.worktrees, or features.tui key among its features.* entries; and the docs Git worktrees page describes worktrees as a shipped feature without ever saying they are default-enabled, so the changelog line is the only first-party statement of that default. The docs “Voice” feature page still documents ChatGPT Voice in the desktop app, a separate surface this guide distinguishes throughout.[169](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:247) v0.155.1 (stable, September 18, 2026, 20:03 UTC; npm latest until 0.156.0) is a one-fix hotfix patch: none is restored as the TUI reasoning-summary default. The rust-v0.155.0…rust-v0.155.1 compare is two commits – the fix and the release-prep commit – and the fix is a single line. On 0.155.0, a new local TUI thread that had no explicit model_reasoning_summary in config fell back to detailed and sent that on the wire, which providers that do not support reasoning summaries rejected outright; 0.155.1 restores the none fallback, so an unset key means no summaries are requested. Explicit auto, concise, and detailed settings were always honored and still are, and the same one-line change landed independently on main as #46533. If you saw new 0.155.0 TUI sessions fail against a non-OpenAI or self-hosted provider, this is the fix; if you deliberately want summaries, set the key (see the config reference).[158](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:244) As of CLI v0.155.0 (stable, September 17, 2026; npm latest until 0.155.1), voice ships – experimental, opt-in, and NOT on by default. Core Layer: The GPT model family powers everything. As of September 2026, gpt-6-astra is the recommended model (rollout announced complete September 4, entitlement still uneven in practice; the bundled default on CLI 0.153.4+ when no model is explicitly configured), with gpt-5.6-sol – the “Power” setting, medium reasoning – as the stable fallback and Terra (everyday) and Luna (fast, affordable) beside it; gpt-5.5 is the previous-generation flagship (400K context in Codex, 1M in the API), and gpt-5.4 retires from Codex on August 31, 2026.[83](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:160)[117](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:201)[146](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:232)[148](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:234)[149](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:235) It reads files, writes patches, executes shell commands, and reasons about your codebase. When context fills, Codex compacts the conversation to free space. This layer costs tokens.
Security Layer: Every command Codex runs passes through an OS-level sandbox. On macOS, Apple’s Seatbelt framework enforces kernel-level restrictions. On Linux, Landlock + seccomp filter filesystem and syscall access. The sandbox operates at the kernel level, not inside containers. The approval policy then decides when to ask for human confirmation.
Extension Layer: MCP connects external services (GitHub, Figma, Sentry). Skills package reusable workflows that Codex loads on demand. Apps connect to ChatGPT connectors. Web search adds real-time context from the internet.
Surface Layer: CLI for terminal power users and automation. Desktop app for multi-threaded project management. IDE extension for edit-compile-test loops. Cloud for async tasks that run independently.
The key insight: Most users only use one surface. Power users use all five: Cloud for long-running tasks, CLI for deterministic repo operations, IDE extension for tight coding loops, the desktop app for planning and coordination, and the browser extension for signed-in browser workflows.

Configuration System Deep Dive
Codex uses TOML for configuration. Understanding the precedence hierarchy is critical because it determines which settings win when they conflict.
Precedence (Highest to Lowest)
Session overrides (highest): CLI flags (--model, --sandbox, --ask-for-approval, --search, --enable/--disable, --profile) and -c key=value overrides
Project config (.codex/config.toml, discovered from CWD upward to project root; closest directory wins)
User config ($CODEX_HOME/config.toml, defaults to ~/.codex/config.toml)
System config (/etc/codex/config.toml on Unix)
Built-in defaults (lowest)
requirements.toml acts as a policy constraint layer that restricts what values users can select after normal config merging. See [Enterprise Deployment](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#enterprise-deployment).

Profiles
Named configuration presets for different work modes. Since Codex 0.134.0 each profile is its own file — ~/.codex/<name>.config.toml, holding top-level keys only — and --profile <name> overlays that file on ~/.codex/config.toml. The older [profiles.<name>] tables inside config.toml and the top-level profile = "<name>" selector are no longer read; a leftover [profiles.<name>] table makes --profile <name> refuse to start until you move its keys into the profile file.[122](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:208)

How Does the Sandbox & Approval System Work?
Codex uses a two-layer security model that separates what is technically possible from when Codex asks for human approval. The approach differs fundamentally from Claude Code’s permission system — Codex enforces restrictions at the OS kernel level.[5](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:5) See also [Enterprise Deployment](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#enterprise-deployment) for requirements.toml constraints that administrators enforce organization-wide.
v0.148.0 hardening: sandbox restrictions now fail closed — a denied or unreadable path is treated as blocked instead of silently allowed — on both Linux and Windows.[118](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:204)

A standalone helper process (codex-linux-sandbox) provides defense-in-depth isolation.[5](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:5) Bubblewrap (bwrap) is vendored and compiled as part of the Linux build (promoted from optional in v0.100.0)[7](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:7). v0.117.0 improved sandbox reliability on older distros with legacy kernel configurations.[75](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:80) v0.129.0 hardened sandbox startup on Linux and bumped vendored Bubblewrap to 0.11.2 with upstream security patches; v0.130.0 added further startup hardening.[89](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:166)[91](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:168)
Windows: Native sandbox with restricted tokens (promoted from experimental in v0.100.0). WSL also supported (inherits Linux Landlock + seccomp). v0.117.0 includes restricted-token sandbox improvements for better process isolation.[75](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:80) v0.130.0 grants sandbox users access to the desktop runtime binary cache so that the Windows sandbox can resolve runtime binaries reliably for workspace-sandbox users.[91](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:168)
Why this matters: Unlike container-based sandboxing (Docker), OS-level sandboxing is faster, lighter, and harder to escape. The kernel enforces restrictions before Codex even sees the system call.

The new --approve-for-me CLI flag turns approval prompts into automatically reviewed approvals: instead of interrupting you, each request is adjudicated by a review pass and approved or refused on your behalf.[116](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:200) This sits between “approve everything” (the posture --full-auto used to encourage, now removed) and “interrupt for everything” — the prompts still exist as decision points, but a reviewer answers them. Pair it with the v0.146.1 safer auto-review defaults for cyber-capable models, which this flag inherits. Treat it like any delegation of authority: right for long unattended runs where interruption means a stall, wrong for sessions touching credentials or production state where you want to be the reviewer.

The write_stdin_approval feature flag – disabled by default – requires a fresh approval before non-empty input is sent to an escalated unified-exec terminal. These reviews route through hooks, Guardian, the app server, and the TUI as writeStdin approvals; the terminal’s environment, launch directory, and escalation state persist across turns, and the process identity is revalidated after approval before any bytes are written. The fully formatted action and approval reason must fit within 8,000 bytes – oversized or truncated actions are rejected before approval is requested or anything reaches the terminal.[135](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:222)

How Does AGENTS.md Work?
AGENTS.md is Codex’s project instruction system — an open standard[9](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:10) now governed by the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation. Supported by Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Amp, Jules (Google), Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Cline, Aider, Zed, Factory, RooCode, and 60,000+ open source projects. It defines how Codex behaves within a specific repository or directory. See [Skills](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#what-are-skills) for reusable expertise packages that complement AGENTS.md.
Discovery Hierarchy
Codex builds an instruction chain at session start by walking the directory tree:
Global (~/.codex/): AGENTS.override.md > AGENTS.md
Project (git root to current directory): Each level checked for AGENTS.override.md > AGENTS.md > fallback filenames
Merging: Files concatenate root-down; closer files appear later in the prompt and override earlier guidance
~/.codex/AGENTS.md ← Global defaults └─ /repo/AGENTS.md ← Project-wide rules └─ /repo/services/AGENTS.md ← Service-specific rules └─ /repo/services/payments/ AGENTS.override.md ← Overrides everything above for this dir
Copy
Untrusted projects skip project AGENTS.md (v0.150.0): the walk above assumes the project is trusted. Since v0.150.0, “Untrusted projects no longer supply project-level AGENTS.md instructions, and managed deny-read rules remain enforced after permission changes” – project-scoped discovery is skipped while user-level ~/.codex/AGENTS.md instructions are preserved, so an untrusted checkout cannot inject an operating contract before you trust it.[132](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:218)
Desktop multi-folder projects (26.715, July 23, 2026): The walk above describes the CLI, which resolves everything relative to the current working directory. The ChatGPT desktop app now lets a local project span several related folders, and it resolves discovery against exactly one of them: “New chats, Git operations, and automatic discovery of AGENTS.md, skills, and config.toml use the primary folder. Secondary folders remain available for file search, reading, and editing.” You choose which folder is primary from the project’s menu via Edit project.[113](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:195)
That single setting governs three of Codex’s five core systems at once — instructions, skills, and configuration all follow the primary folder. Practically: an AGENTS.md in a secondary folder is a file Codex can open, not an operating contract it loads. If the repo carrying your rules is the one you attached second, either promote it to primary or restate those rules in the primary folder’s AGENTS.md; the same applies to repository skill folders you expected to be picked up. Nothing about the CLI’s directory walk changed — this is desktop-app project scoping.
What Makes a Great AGENTS.md
Based on direct guidance from Codex itself and community patterns[10](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:11):
DO:
Be specific: "Use rg --files for discovery" beats "search efficiently"
Define closure: What does “done” mean? (tests pass, lint clean, etc.)
Include commands: Build, test, lint, format (exact invocations)
Organize by task: Coding, review, release, incident/debug sections
Define escalation: What to do when blocked or encountering unexpected state
DON’T:
Dump entire style guides without execution rules
Use ambiguous directives (“be careful,” “optimize”)
Mix contradictory priorities (speed + exhaustive verification + no runtime budget)

Hooks are organized in three levels – an event, a matcher group, and one or more handlers – and live either in hooks.json (~/.codex/hooks.json, <repo>/.codex/hooks.json, or a plugin’s hooks/hooks.json) or inline in config.toml and requirements.toml. Project-local hooks load only when the project .codex/ layer is trusted.[124](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:210) The inline TOML form:
# ~/.codex/config.toml or <repo>/.codex/config.toml [[hooks.SessionStart]] matcher = "startup|resume" [[hooks.SessionStart.hooks]] type = "command" command = "python3 ~/.codex/hooks/session_start.py" additionalContextLimit = 5000 [[hooks.PreToolUse]] matcher = "^Bash$" [[hooks.PreToolUse.hooks]] type = "command" command = '/usr/bin/python3 "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.codex/hooks/pre_tool_use_policy.py"' timeout = 30 statusMessage = "Checking Bash command" [[hooks.PostToolUse]] matcher = "^Bash$" [[hooks.PostToolUse.hooks]] type = "command" command = "python3 ~/.codex/hooks/post_tool_use_review.py" async = true timeout = 120

Commands run with the session cwd as their working directory, so repo-local hooks should resolve paths from git rev-parse --show-toplevel rather than a relative .codex/hooks/... path.[124](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:210)
Review and trust. Codex records trust against each non-managed hook’s current hash; new or changed hooks are marked for review and skipped until trusted. Run /hooks to inspect hook sources, review, trust, or disable individual hooks; when hooks need review at startup, Codex prints a warning pointing at /hooks. Managed hooks from system, MDM, cloud, or requirements.toml sources are trusted by policy and cannot be disabled from the user hook browser. --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust runs enabled hooks without persisted trust for one invocation, for automation that vets hook sources elsewhere.[124](https://blakecrosley.com/guides/codex#fn:210)
The SessionStart hook’s stdout feeds into the model’s context, making it ideal for injecting dynamic information (dates, branch names, environment variables) at session start.

# Implementation Plan: Codex CLI Setup for CogainCore

Setup and standardize Codex CLI (`@openai/codex`) configuration for the `cogain-core` repository based on the comprehensive 2026 Codex reference guide (v0.156.0). We will migrate and optimize the existing `.agents/` instructions, rules, and skills into Codex's canonical discovery paths.

## Proposed Architecture & Directory Structure

Codex CLI relies on 5 core pillars:
1. **`AGENTS.md` (Project Operating Contract)**: Discovered hierarchically by walking from root downward.
   - Root: `/AGENTS.md` (Global project rules, tech stack, CLI commands, secret handling, closure definition).
   - Frontend: `/frontend/AGENTS.md` (React 19 + TypeScript + TanStack Router/Query + Radix/Tailwind rules migrated from `react-typescript-rules.md`).
   - Backend: `/backend/AGENTS.md` (.NET 9 + Microservices + EF Core + BaseService/Controller + Snapshot Policy patterns).
2. **Configuration (`.codex/config.toml` & Profiles)**:
   - `.codex/config.toml`: Base project config (model fallback `gpt-5.6-sol`, reasoning `medium`, `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`, `approval_policy = "on-request"`, shell env secret exclusion, feature flags).
   - `.codex/fast.config.toml`: Fast profile (`gpt-5.6-luna`, reasoning `low`).
   - `.codex/careful.config.toml`: Deep analysis & security profile (`gpt-5.5`, reasoning `xhigh`, `read-only`).
   - `.codex/ci.config.toml`: Automated headless profile (`gpt-5.6-luna`, `approval_policy = "never"`).
3. **Skills (`skills/` directory at root)**:
   - Codex discovers skills at `./skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.
   - Copy all relevant and active skills from `.agents/skills/` into `./skills/` so they are immediately accessible in Codex via `$skill-name`, `/skills`, or automatic prompt description matching.
4. **Hooks (`.codex/hooks.json`)**:
   - Provide lifecycle hooks including protection against running `dotnet ef` migrations, session startup info, and post-tool linting options.

---

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Codex Configuration (`.codex/`)

#### [NEW] [config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/config.toml)
- Define `model = "gpt-5.6-sol"`, `model_reasoning_effort = "medium"`.
- Set `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"` and `approval_policy = "on-request"`.
- Configure `[shell_environment_policy]` to exclude sensitive credentials (`*KEY*`, `*SECRET*`, `*TOKEN*`, `*PASSWORD*`, `*AUTH*`).
- Configure `project_root_markers = [".git", "pnpm-workspace.yaml", "backend/CogainSolution.sln"]`.
- Configure `project_doc_fallback_filenames = [".agents/AGENTS.md"]`.
- Enable standard features (`shell_tool`, `unified_exec`, `goals`, `hooks`, `plugins`, `prevent_idle_sleep`).

#### [NEW] Profiles:
- [fast.config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/fast.config.toml): Routine edits and fast tests.
- [careful.config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/careful.config.toml): Security audits & architectural review.
- [ci.config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/ci.config.toml): CI/CD automation without prompts.

#### [NEW] [hooks.json](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/hooks.json)
- PreToolUse hook configuration and safety guardrails.

---

### 2. Hierarchical AGENTS.md Operating Contracts

#### [NEW] [AGENTS.md](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/AGENTS.md) (Project Root)
Consolidates the global project contract:
- **Build / Test / Lint Commands**: Full list of pnpm commands for frontend packages and dotnet commands for backend.
- **Strict Project Invariants**:
  - NEVER execute automatic EF migrations (`dotnet ef migrations add`, `dotnet ef database update`).
  - Strict Ban on Raw HTML form tags (`<select>`, `<input type="date">`, `<table>`, etc.) -> Use shared components.
  - Mandatory custom hooks for API calls (NO inline `useQuery`/`useMutation` in components).
  - Ticket Slideout Sheet 85% width rule.
  - Ticket filter popovers and detail table search/filter popovers.
  - Strict Zero Hardcoded Text Rule (`useTranslation` with `defaultValue`).
- **Security & Secret Handling**: Prevent leaking secrets into session history or shell snapshots.
- **Closure Criteria (Definition of Done)**: Exact conditions for completing tasks.

#### [NEW] [frontend/AGENTS.md](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/frontend/AGENTS.md)
Inherited automatically by Codex whenever operating in `frontend/`:
- Complete React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + TanStack guidelines adapted from `react-typescript-rules.md`.
- Detail table standards (`ResizableWrapTable`, `SortableWrapTable`, `CustomTable`).
- Filter popover patterns, Sheet 85% width implementation, Zod schema validation, i18n conventions.

#### [NEW] [backend/AGENTS.md](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/backend/AGENTS.md)
Inherited automatically by Codex whenever operating in `backend/`:
- Complete .NET 9 microservice guidelines adapted from `cogain-backend-crud` and `api-backend`.
- `record` declarations for entities and DTOs, `EntityAuditBase<Guid>`, GuidV7, `DateTimeOffset`.
- Consolidated DTO structure, `[AutoFilter]`, BaseService / BaseController patterns, Ocelot Gateway routes in `appsettings.json`.
- Strict manual migration rule.

---

### 3. Skills Migration (`skills/`)

#### [NEW] [skills/](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/skills)
- Copy all 70 skills from `.agents/skills/` into the project root `skills/` directory.
- This ensures Codex CLI natively detects every skill via `/skills`, `$skill-name`, and semantic task matching, while keeping existing `.agents/skills` untouched for backward compatibility with other tools.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Verification
1. Verify directory structure and files:
   - Check `.codex/config.toml` exists and is valid TOML syntax.
   - Check `AGENTS.md`, `frontend/AGENTS.md`, `backend/AGENTS.md` exist.
   - Verify `skills/` contains the migrated skills with `SKILL.md` files intact.
2. Run validation checks:
   - `pnpm lint` or package check to confirm workspace integrity is preserved.
   - Run a test script to verify `config.toml` parsing and skill count.

### Manual Verification
- Review generated TOML and Markdown files against Blake Crosley's guide standards.

# CogainCore Project Operating Contract (AGENTS.md) This is the primary operating contract for AI agents (Codex CLI, Cursor, Copilot, etc.) working on the `cogain-core` codebase. All instructions and constraints defined herein are non-negotiable and strictly enforced. --- ## 1. Project Architecture & Monorepo Overview `cogain-core` is an enterprise ERP / HRM / CRM platform composed of two core tiers: - **Backend (`/backend`)**: ASP.NET Core (.NET 9) microservices architecture (`HR`, `MasterData`, `ServiceDesk`, `WorkFlow`, `BusinessDocument`, `ERP`, `Reporting`) using Entity Framework Core, PostgreSQL, GuidV7, AutoFilter, and Ocelot API Gateway. - **Frontend (`/frontend`)**: Modern React 19 + TypeScript monorepo managed via `pnpm` workspaces (`bizdoc`, `crm`, `erp`, `helpdesk`, `hrm`, `interactive`, `workflow`, `shared`), built with Vite, `@tanstack/react-router`, `@tanstack/react-query` v5, TailwindCSS v4, and Radix UI / shadcn. For detailed domain-specific instructions, Codex automatically loads: - [frontend/AGENTS.md](frontend/AGENTS.md): Full React 19, TypeScript, TanStack, and UI styling specifications. - [backend/AGENTS.md](backend/AGENTS.md): Full .NET 9 microservice, EF Core, entity, and controller specifications. --- ## 2. Common Build, Dev, Test & Lint Commands ### Frontend (`/frontend` via root `pnpm`) - **Start Dev Server for a package**: - BizDoc: `pnpm bizdoc dev` - CRM: `pnpm crm dev` - ERP: `pnpm erp dev` - HR: `pnpm --filter @cogain/hrm dev` - Interactive: `pnpm inter dev` - Workflow: `pnpm workflow dev` - HelpDesk: `pnpm helpdesk dev` - **Lint all frontend apps**: `pnpm lint` - **Auto-fix lint errors**: `pnpm lint:fix` - **Typecheck**: `pnpm --filter [package-name] typecheck` ### Backend (`/backend` via `dotnet CLI`) - **Build Entire Solution**: `dotnet build backend/CogainSolution.sln` - **Build Specific Service**: `dotnet build backend/src/Services/[ServiceName]/[ServiceName].API` - **Run Tests**: `dotnet test backend/CogainSolution.sln` - **Merge Ocelot Gateway Config**: `node backend/merge-ocelot.js` --- ## 3. Mandatory Non-Negotiable Project Rules ### 3.1. Database Migrations (CRITICAL) - **NEVER** run Entity Framework migration commands automatically (e.g., `dotnet ef migrations add`, `dotnet ef database update`). - The generation and execution of migrations must strictly be left to the developer to execute manually. - When scaffolding or modifying entities, do not attempt to run or update database migrations on behalf of the user. ### 3.2. Frontend Data Fetching & Service Encapsulation - **NEVER** call API services directly or write raw inline `useQuery`/`useMutation` inside UI components, `.tsx` files, or route pages (e.g. `service.getPaged(...)`, `service.exportData()`, `service.create(...)`). - All data queries and mutations **MUST** be encapsulated inside dedicated custom hooks (`use`). UI components only consume the hook. - Data export **MUST** use `exportDataMutation.mutateAsync` followed by `useFile().downloadFile(...)` and `toastSuccess`. **NEVER** use raw `window.open(res.data)`. ### 3.3. Strict Ban on Raw HTML Form Controls (Use Shared Components) - **NEVER** use raw native HTML form tags: ``, ``, ``, or raw `//
`. - **MANDATORY**: Always utilize pre-built project components from `@shared/components` and `@shared/ui`: - **Dropdowns / Selects**: `CustomSelect`, `LazyCombobox`, `Combobox`, `CustomMultiSelect`, `TreeSelect`. - **Date & Time**: `DatePicker` (from `@shared/components/custom/date-picker`), `DateRangeInput`. - **Numeric & Text Inputs**: `NumericInput`, `Input`, `DebouncedInput`. - **Tables**: `ResizableWrapTable`, `SortableWrapTable`, `CustomTable`. ### 3.4. Ticket & List Page Filter Standards - **NEVER** place raw inline filter controls or ad-hoc select toolbars directly in the page header. - **MANDATORY**: Build a dedicated `<[Ticket]FilterPopover>` component using `FilterPopoverLayout` (from `@shared/components`) or `Popover` (from `@shared/ui`) with active filter count badge, clearable options, and Reset/Apply actions (modeled after `AcceptanceMinuteFilterPopover`). ### 3.5. Ticket Slideout Form Standards (85% Width Rule) - **MANDATORY**: Form components for business tickets and request documents ("Phiếu") must **NEVER** be modal dialogs. They must always use a slideout `Sheet` (`side="right"`) standardized to **85% width**: ```tsx e.preventDefault()} > ``` ### 3.6. Mandatory Detail Table Search & Filter Popover - **EVERY** child and detail table **MUST** have both search and filter configured on `ResizableWrapTable` via `toolbarProps`. - The detail filter **MUST** render as a wide multi-column form popover: `renderFilterContent: (close) =>
` with responsive grid (`grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-3 gap-4`) and Reset / Apply buttons. ### 3.7. Strict Zero Hardcoded Text Rule (MANDATORY i18n) - **NEVER** hardcode text strings anywhere in UI components, JSX, or table column configurations (e.g., `header: 'Loại hình'`, `

`, ``, ``, placeholders, toasts). - **EVERY** single string visible to users **MUST** be localized using `useTranslation` with proper namespaces and fallback `defaultValue`: ```tsx t('namespace:key', { defaultValue: 'Default Text' }) ``` --- ## 4. Secret Handling & Agent Session Hygiene - **NEVER** print, log, or commit passwords, API keys, tokens, or connection strings in code, PRs, transcripts, or terminal outputs. - Database credentials and secrets are managed exclusively through `.env` files or secure environment variables. - All sensitive environment variable patterns (`*KEY*`, `*SECRET*`, `*TOKEN*`, `*PASSWORD*`, `*AUTH*`) are excluded from Codex shell snapshots. --- ## 5. Definition of Done & Task Closure A task is considered complete when: 1. All changes adhere strictly to the project rules defined in this file and child `AGENTS.md` files. 2. Code compiles cleanly without TypeScript, linter, or C# errors (`pnpm lint`, `dotnet build`). 3. For Frontend: - UI forms use 85% width slideout sheet for tickets. - All text uses `useTranslation` with fallback `defaultValue`. - Data mutations use encapsulated custom hooks. - Tables use `ResizableWrapTable` / `SortableWrapTable` with `toolbarProps`. 4. For Backend: - Entities and DTOs use `record` syntax and inherit `EntityAuditBase`. - Migration scripts are NOT executed; user is informed if a migration is required. - Routes and DI are cleanly configured. --- ## 6. Escalation Protocol If you encounter: - Ambiguous requirements or conflicting domain logic: Stop, explain the trade-offs, and ask the user for clarification. - An unexpected database schema mismatch: Point out the issue and suggest the entity/configuration changes without running migrations. - Missing shared components: Inspect `@shared/components` or `@shared/ui` before creating any new abstractions.

# Backend Operating Guidelines (.NET 9 Microservices)

This document governs all backend development within `cogain-core` (`backend/src/Services/*`, `backend/src/BuildingBlocks/*`). It is automatically merged with root `AGENTS.md`.

---

## 1. Core Architecture & Tech Stack

- **Framework:** .NET 9 / ASP.NET Core Web API.
- **ORM & Database:** Entity Framework Core + PostgreSQL with `SnakeCaseNamingConvention`.
- **Primary Keys:** GuidV7 auto-generated via `EntityAuditBase<Guid>`.
- **Date/Time:** Always use `DateTimeOffset`, never raw `DateTime`.
- **API Gateway:** Ocelot Gateway with route discovery managed through `CacheKeys` in microservice `appsettings.json`.

---

## 2. Mandatory Backend Development Rules

### 2.1. Database Migrations (CRITICAL)
- **NEVER** execute migration commands automatically:
  - ❌ `dotnet ef migrations add ...`
  - ❌ `dotnet ef database update ...`
- All database migration creation and execution must be left strictly for the human developer to run manually.
- When scaffolding or updating entities, notify the developer of schema changes needed.

### 2.2. Entity Declaration Standards
- **Use `record` Syntax:** Declare entities as `public record [EntityName] : EntityAuditBase<Guid>` (or `WorkItemEntityAuditBase<Guid>` for WorkItem tickets).
- **Auto-generated Id:** Never declare `public Guid Id { get; set; }` inside the entity as it is already defined in `EntityAuditBase<Guid>`.
- **Attributes:**
  - Add `[AutoFilter]` to enable automatic filtering and sorting via `AutoFilterService`.
  - Add `[CodeGeneration("[Description]", EContextScope.[Microservice], typeof([EntityName]))]`.
- **Unit of Measure:** Use `UomId` (never `UnitId`).
- **Soft Deletes:** Managed via `DeletedDate`. Never hard-delete records.

### 2.3. EF Core Entity Configuration
File: `backend/src/Services/[Microservice]/[Microservice].Data/Persistence/Configurations/[FeatureName]/[EntityName]Configuration.cs`
- Table naming in lowercase/snake_case: `builder.ToTable("[entity_names]");`
- Primary key: `builder.HasKey(x => x.Id);`
- Unique code index with soft-delete filter:
  ```csharp
  builder.HasIndex(x => x.Code)
      .IsUnique()
      .HasFilter("\"deleted_date\" IS NULL");
  ```

### 2.4. Consolidated DTO File Standard
All DTO records for an entity must reside in a single file:
`backend/src/BuildingBlocks/Shared/Dto/[Microservice]/[FeatureName]/[EntityName]Dto.cs`
```csharp
public record [EntityName]Dto : BaseDto<Guid> { ... }
public record Create[EntityName]Dto { ... }
public record Update[EntityName]Dto { ... }
public record CreateAndUpdate[EntityName]Dto { ... }
public record [EntityName]FilterPaging : FilterPagingModel { ... }
```

### 2.5. Service & Controller Architecture
- **Service Interface:** Inherits `IBaseService<Guid, [EntityName]Dto, Create[EntityName]Dto, Update[EntityName]Dto, [EntityName]FilterPaging>`.
- **Service Implementation:** Inherits `BaseService<[EntityName], Guid, [EntityName]Dto, Create[EntityName]Dto, Update[EntityName]Dto, [EntityName]FilterPaging>`.
- **Controller:** Inherits `BaseController<...>` or `BaseExcelController<...>` if Excel import/export is required.

### 2.6. API Gateway Route Registration
- Add the entity to `"CacheKeys"` in `appsettings.json` of the target microservice API project.
- Run `node backend/merge-ocelot.js` if updating Ocelot configuration across services.

---

## 3. Scaffolding File Layout for New CRUD APIs

When scaffolding a new CRUD API for `[EntityName]` in `[Microservice]`:
1. **Entity**: `backend/src/Services/[Microservice]/[Microservice].Data/Entities/[FeatureName]/[EntityName].cs`
2. **Configuration**: `backend/src/Services/[Microservice]/[Microservice].Data/Persistence/Configurations/[FeatureName]/[EntityName]Configuration.cs`
3. **DTOs**: `backend/src/BuildingBlocks/Shared/Dto/[Microservice]/[FeatureName]/[EntityName]Dto.cs`
4. **Service Interface**: `backend/src/Services/[Microservice]/[Microservice].Services/Interface/[FeatureName]/I[EntityName]Service.cs`
5. **Service Implementation**: `backend/src/Services/[Microservice]/[Microservice].Services/Implement/[FeatureName]/[EntityName]Service.cs`
6. **Controller**: `backend/src/Services/[Microservice]/[Microservice].API/Controllers/[FeatureName]/[EntityName]sController.cs`

# Codex CLI Setup Walkthrough for CogainCore

Đã hoàn thành thiết lập môi trường và cấu hình dự án toàn diện cho **Codex CLI** (`@openai/codex` v0.156.0) theo chuẩn tài liệu tham khảo 2026 của Blake Crosley.

---

## Các thành phần đã triển khai

### 1. Hệ thống cấu hình Codex (`.codex/`)
- [config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/config.toml): Cấu hình base cho dự án:
  - **Model:** `gpt-5.6-sol` (phân hạng "Power", reasoning level `medium`) làm fallback ổn định.
  - **Sandbox & Quyền:** `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`, `approval_policy = "on-request"`.
  - **Bảo mật môi trường:** Che giấu các biến môi trường nhạy cảm (`*KEY*`, `*SECRET*`, `*TOKEN*`, `*PASSWORD*`, `*AUTH*`, `DATABASE_URL`, `CONNECTION_STRING`).
  - **Nhận diện Root:** Nhận diện `.git`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `backend/CogainSolution.sln`.
- **Profiles (`.codex/<name>.config.toml`)**:
  - [fast.config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/fast.config.toml): Sử dụng `gpt-5.6-luna` với `low` reasoning cho tác vụ nhanh, format, sửa lỗi nhỏ.
  - [careful.config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/careful.config.toml): Sử dụng `gpt-5.5` với `xhigh` reasoning, `read-only` sandbox cho audit bảo mật và thiết kế kiến trúc.
  - [ci.config.toml](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/ci.config.toml): Dành cho headless CI/CD với `approval_policy = "never"`.
- [hooks.json](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/.codex/hooks.json):
  - PreToolUse hook tự động chặn các lệnh tự động chạy migration EF (`dotnet ef migrations add`, `dotnet ef database update`).

---

### 2. Cây chỉ thị phân cấp (Hierarchical `AGENTS.md`)
Codex CLI tự động duyệt và gộp các file `AGENTS.md` theo cấu trúc thư mục từ trên xuống dưới:
- [AGENTS.md (Root)](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/AGENTS.md):
  - Kiến trúc tổng thể Monorepo (.NET microservices + React 19 pnpm workspaces).
  - Lệnh dev, build, lint, test cho cả frontend và backend.
  - 7 quy tắc cốt lõi bắt buộc: nghiêm cấm tự chạy EF migration, custom hook bắt buộc cho API, cấm dùng raw HTML form controls, chuẩn FilterPopover, chuẩn slideout Sheet 85% width cho phiếu, chuẩn bảng chi tiết có search/filter, chuẩn bắt buộc i18n không hardcode text.
  - Quy tắc bảo mật secrets và tiêu chuẩn nghiệm thu (Definition of Done).
- [frontend/AGENTS.md](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/frontend/AGENTS.md):
  - Kế thừa tự động khi Codex làm việc trong thư mục `frontend/`.
  - Quy chuẩn React 19 + TypeScript strict mode, Zod inference, Radix/Tailwind components, `ResizableWrapTable`, `SortableWrapTable`, `ResourceVersionBadge`.
- [backend/AGENTS.md](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/backend/AGENTS.md):
  - Kế thừa tự động khi Codex làm việc trong thư mục `backend/`.
  - Quy chuẩn C# 12+ `record` syntax, `EntityAuditBase<Guid>`, GuidV7, `DateTimeOffset`, DTO hợp nhất, `[AutoFilter]`, `BaseService`, BaseController, và định tuyến Ocelot qua `appsettings.json`.

---

### 3. Di chuyển Skills (`skills/`)
- Đã sao chép toàn bộ **70 skills** từ `.agents/skills/` sang thư mục gốc [skills/](file:///c:/Users/Admin/Desktop/CogainCore/cogain-core/skills) theo đúng vị trí khám phá mặc định của Codex CLI.
- Bao gồm các skills đặc thù dự án:
  - `cogain-frontend-crud`, `cogain-backend-crud`, `cogain-frontend-master-data`, `cogain-request-ticket`, `cogain-backend-cross-service-table`, `api-backend`.
- Các skills chất lượng cao:
  - Bộ `antislop*`, `code-review*`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `tdd`, `frontend-design`, `improve-ui`, `vercel-react-best-practices`, `brainstorming`,...

---

## Hướng dẫn sử dụng với Codex CLI

1. **Khởi chạy Codex bình thường:**
   ```bash
   codex
   ```
2. **Khởi chạy với Profile cụ thể:**
   ```bash
   codex --profile fast "Sửa style cho bảng chi tiết packing list"
   codex --profile careful "Audit bảo mật cho auth endpoint"
   ```
3. **Kích hoạt Skill trong phiên làm việc:**
   - Dùng lệnh slash `/skills` hoặc gõ trực tiếp tên skill: `$cogain-frontend-crud`, `$cogain-request-ticket`, `$antislop`,...
   - Hoặc Codex sẽ tự động match skill theo mô tả tác vụ trong prompt của bạn.
4. **Kiểm tra cấu hình Codex:**
   ```bash
   codex /status
   codex /debug-config
   ```
